stage1.impression: A moody, nearly photographic rain scene: the streaks, the wet black ground and the puddle mirror are convincing, and the low bright band behind gives the frame real depth. But the speaker is a backlit, underexposed mustard-brown block against the brightest part of the sky, so the golden acrylic never glows and it reads as a dull object rather than the hero. The splash crowns around its foot are a field of near-identical bright beads that say 'render', the sky is a pale overcast rather than a storm, and the lime-green ridge on the left looks tinted.

blocking_9: Cabinet front face reads as luminous golden amber, brighter than the ground and close to the horizon band: lum_median 110 to 150 in [510,370,560,560], with the blue channel not crushed to 0
Sky reads as a storm: the cloud deck clearly darker than the horizon band (upper sky lum_median 110 to 145, horizon band under 205)
Splashes read as random, varied water, not a grid of identical bright beads; no visible edge where the splash field ends
Light through the tinted acrylic visible: a lit right edge or glow on the side panel and its coloured light falling on the water at the foot
Far ridge and far field neutral grey-olive under the haze, not lime green; no flat featureless band at the horizon

defects.what: Cabinet underexposed and backlit: front face lum_median 74, RGB 104/73/0; reads mustard-brown, no glow through the acrylic
Right side of the cabinet falls to lum_median 44; the rim card does not register as an edge light
Woofer area nearly black (lum_median 19), a dark hole in the hero
Upper sky is a pale overcast (lum_median 181), not a dark storm deck; little drama
Horizon band at lum 233, the brightest area in the frame; it pulls the eye off the product and silhouettes it
Splash crowns are bright, similar-sized white beads arranged densely in the reflection; read as repeated CG instances
Splash field ends visibly at about 3 m; beyond it, no splashes on the puddle
Left ridge rendered lime green by the haze colour; looks tinted, not real rock in rain
Far field reads as a flat, smooth grey band between the rock and the ridge; low detail
Wet rock on the right carries bright specular glints (p95 203) that compete with the product
Foot of the cabinet merges into the splash field; contact with the water is not defined

changes.problem: The cabinet's front face is underexposed and the golden acrylic reads as mustard-brown.

evidence.measured: lum_median 74, RGB median 104/73/0, against a sky behind at 221 to 233

change.setting: 2 m reflector, 70 deg to the camera's left
change.to: irradiance 4.0, moved to 40 deg left of the camera axis at cabinet mid-height, colour kept #F1E6B8

changes.expected: Front face lifts by about one stop to a luminous golden yellow, the white lining visible through the acrylic; the face is the brightest saturated area in the frame

changes.problem: The sky is a pale overcast, not a storm, and the horizon band is the brightest thing in the frame.

evidence.measured: upper sky lum_median 181; horizon band [850,300,1200,420] lum_median 233

change.to: 0.13 (sun lamp kept at 10.0 so the rim and streak light hold)

changes.expected: The cloud deck goes dark slate-olive, the low band stays as a glowing break but no longer outshines the product

changes.problem: The rim card does not register; the right side of the cabinet is dark and the acrylic shows no edge glow.

change.setting: 1.5 m card behind right toward the sun
change.to: 9.0, moved 20 deg further behind so it grazes the right side panel and transmits through the acrylic edge

changes.expected: A bright amber line down the right edge and light through the side panel, separating the cabinet from the sky

changes.problem: The splash crowns read as a dense field of identical bright beads, and the field ends visibly.

evidence.measured: lum_p95 131.5 with repeated near-identical bright specks; no splashes past about x 1000 on the puddle

change.from: 1,200 crowns 3 to 14 mm within about 3 m, opacity 0.25
change.to: 700 crowns within 3 m plus 900 within 3 to 10 m, sizes 2 to 25 mm on a log distribution, opacity drawn per crown 0.06 to 0.2, each rotated and scaled randomly

changes.expected: Sparse, varied splashes that thin with distance; the reflection of the cabinet reads through them

changes.problem: The cabinet's blue channel is crushed to zero, which turns the golden amber olive-brown.

change.to: AgX Base Contrast, tint -6; finish contrast 0.22 to 0.15 to keep the shadows open

changes.expected: Amber holds a clean yellow without going brown; overall frame still greenish but less sour

changes.problem: The haze colour paints the far ridge lime green and the far field is a flat band.

evidence.measured: ridge visibly lime-saturated in a 2x crop; far band [0,430,1200,450] lum_median 125 with little texture

change.to: 0.0025 /m, #A9AE84 (less saturated); and break the far field with the coarse rock at 1.5 m a tile and more of the 45 to 150 m blocks

changes.expected: The ridge sits grey-olive behind rain and haze; the horizon recedes in steps rather than a flat strip

changes.problem: Bright specular glints on the wet rock at right compete with the product.

change.to: 0.06 to 0.16, with the clear coat 0.6 to 0.45 on the near-right rock

changes.expected: The rock stays wet but the glints drop, so the brightest specular in the lower frame is the puddle mirror

changes.problem: The woofer is a black hole and the cabinet throws no coloured light onto the water at its foot.

evidence.measured: lum_median 19.4; puddle at the foot [500,620,700,800] r/g/b 75/63/33, little amber

change.setting: Small 0.5 m card low in front
change.to: keep it, and add a second 0.5 m card low in front at 1.5 aimed at the cabinet's lower half

changes.expected: The woofer cone shows its surround and texture; the lower cabinet glows and its amber shows in the puddle reflection

out_of_scope.request: The horn's tinted resin shows a dark, liquid-looking blob inside that reads as melted plastic at this size
out_of_scope.why: It is the speaker's own horn and waveguide shape; only its lighting may change (c8 keeps the throat card)
